title: 启动阶段内存控制：冷启动峰值、预加载与缓存时机
key_conclusions: Startup memory peaks must be split by launch phase and memory bucket instead of judged from one PSS number.
Zygote shared pages, dex/oat mappings, Java heap, Native heap, bitmap pixels, and Graphics buffers require separate evidence.
Preload belongs before first draw only when the first screen cannot function without it.
A peak reduction is valid only if first interaction, PSI, GC, and graphics behavior do not regress.
shallow_points: The article does not include a real Perfetto startup trace or Android Studio allocation recording.
It does not validate exact first-draw and process-start markers across Android versions.
It does not include real zygote shared-page PSS examples.
It does not quantify cache warmup tradeoffs with measured first-interaction latency.

Day 70 should reuse the peak timing model for RecyclerView prefetch, pools, and image decode.
